senses.gloss: डम् डम्, cl. 1. P. डमति, &c., to sound.

डम डम, अस्, m. a despised mixed caste
(commonly Ḍom), the son of a Cāṇḍālī and a Leṭa,
employed to clear away filth &c.

डमर डमर, अस्, आ, m. f. a riot, tumult,
affray, a conflict without weapons; terrifying an
enemy by shouts and gestures; petty or predatory
warfare carried on by detachments or between
villages and not kings; (अम्), n. flight, rout, running
away through fear; [cf. डामर.]

डामर डामर, अस्, m. affray, riot, conflict
without weapons &c. [cf. डमर]; rout, uproar,
the bustle and confusion of festivity or strife; any
surprising thing, sight, or occurrence; a N. common
to six Tantras, viz. the Yoga-ḍāmara, Śiva-ḍ˚, Durgā-
ḍ˚, Sārasvata-ḍ˚, Brahma-ḍ˚, and Gandharva-ḍ˚; N.
of one of the attendants of Śiva; N. of a race or
mixed caste; (अस्, आ, अम्), riotous; [cf. उड्-डामर.]
—डामर-त्व, अम्, n. the state of one who excites
awe.

डमरिन् डमरिन्, ई, m. (?) a sort of drum,
= the next.

डमरु, उस्, m. a musical instrument, a sort of
small drum shaped like an hour-glass and held in one
hand; anything surprising, any strange occurrence &c.
डमरुक, अम्, n. a kind of drum.

डम्प् डम्प्, cl. 10. A. डम्पयते, &c. (a
various reading for डप्), to heap together.

डम्ब् डम्ब्, cl. 10. P. डम्बयति, &c., to
throw, cast, send; order.

डम्बर डम्बर, अस्, m., N. of one of the
attendants of Skanda; an assemblage, collection,
mass; (अस्, आ, अम्), famous, renowned.

डम्भ् डम्भ्, cl. 10. A. डम्भयते, &c.
(various reading for डप्), to collect.
